sellerProfile.category: Agentic infrastructure and developer platform for building, deploying, scaling, and securing web apps, AI apps, agents, and platforms.
valueProps: Fully managed infrastructure designed to scale dynamically with traffic and a global edge for fast site delivery to customers.
Enterprise governance manages, monitors, and governs every app, agent, and workflow from a single enterprise control plane.
Enterprise security includes centralized spend and access controls, RBAC across teams, projects, users, and agents, deployment protection, secure networking, BYOC, and audit trails.
Platform engineering teams can automate infrastructure provisioning, deployment, and monitoring to reduce manual errors.
Preview deployments let teams share live, production-grade environments for faster collaboration and delivery.
Design engineering teams can use live preview environments, preview comments, Vercel Toolbar checks, feature flags, and instant rollbacks to iterate and ship safely.
Multi-tenant SaaS teams can build hosted products that create, deploy, and operate web applications for customers or teams.
Vercel supports AI features with AI Gateway, AI SDK, Sandbox, durable workflows, Fluid Compute, and hundreds of models.

techStack.label: Modern web and AI build stack
techStack.description: Company shows adoption of frameworks, monorepos, AI coding workflows, or frontend architecture patterns that map to Vercel’s strengths.

rubric.1: Little evidence of modern frontend, AI, or product engineering stack.
rubric.3: Uses React/Next.js or similar frameworks in parts of the business, with some public engineering evidence.
rubric.5: Actively hiring or publishing around Next.js, AI agents, monorepos, preview workflows, or high-velocity frontend delivery.

activePain.label: Shipping speed, performance, scaling, or governance pain
activePain.description: Observable signs that teams need to ship faster, reduce infrastructure drag, handle traffic spikes, govern deployments, or improve web performance.

rubric.1: No visible urgency around shipping speed, performance, traffic, or deployment governance.
rubric.3: Some evidence of web performance, launch velocity, or scaling initiatives.
rubric.5: Clear current initiative or pain: traffic spikes, performance targets, rapid product launches, internal app sprawl, custom-domain scaling, or deployment governance.

revenueSensitivity.label: Revenue tied to digital experience
revenueSensitivity.description: Degree to which faster pages, reliable releases, or rapid web iteration directly affects revenue, conversion, user retention, or enterprise productivity.

rubric.1: Website or app is not materially tied to revenue or user engagement.
rubric.3: Digital experience supports acquisition, support, or retention but is not the main monetization path.
rubric.5: Web app/storefront is central to revenue, conversion, usage, or mission-critical customer workflows.

observabilityScale.label: Scale requiring visibility and control
observabilityScale.description: Evidence that the prospect has enough traffic, deployments, teams, or usage-based spend to need observability, spend controls, security controls, and enterprise support.

rubric.1: Small or low-traffic web presence with little need for controls.
rubric.3: Growing product team with meaningful traffic, multiple environments, or compliance needs.
rubric.5: Large-scale usage, frequent deployments, global traffic, regulated requirements, or explicit SLA/security needs.

aiCompatibility.label: AI-assisted software delivery readiness
aiCompatibility.description: Signals that the company is building AI features or using AI coding agents where sandboxing, model access, governed deployment, and rapid iteration matter.
negativeKeywords: AI policy prohibits all AI tools

rubric.1: No sign of AI product development or AI-assisted engineering.
rubric.3: Experimenting with AI features or coding assistants in isolated teams.
rubric.5: Shipping AI features, agent workflows, or AI-generated code into production with governance or scale needs.

competitiveWedge.label: Desire to avoid infrastructure buildout
competitiveWedge.description: Company expresses need to reduce custom DevOps work, avoid building internal deployment tooling, or move faster without adding infrastructure headcount.
evidenceKeywords: platform work becomes a second product
negativeKeywords: built internal deployment system as core differentiator
cloud cost optimization by moving off managed services

rubric.1: Strong preference for owning infrastructure or no stated infrastructure burden.
rubric.3: Some signs of DevOps burden or desire for improved developer experience.
rubric.5: Explicit pain around infrastructure drag, internal tooling cost, staging complexity, or lack of DevOps capacity.

solvingInHouse: built an internal deployment system that is positioned as a strategic differentiator
maintains a dedicated internal preview-environment service with broad adoption
publicly states it is moving deployment and hosting fully in-house
operates its own edge delivery layer as a core product capability
buildCulture: infrastructure team is branded as a product organization for internal web hosting
engineering posts emphasize self-hosting as a company principle
large team dedicated to custom CI/CD, release orchestration, and web runtime operations
open sourced an internal deployment or edge runtime framework and continues to invest in it

pitch.receiptOpenerStyle: Open with a specific observable trigger: a launch deadline, Next.js hiring, Core Web Vitals initiative, traffic spike, custom-domain scaling project, AI-agent production push, or internal-app delivery program.
pitch.oneSentenceProduct: Vercel provides fully managed infrastructure with dynamic scaling, global edge delivery, enterprise governance, security, observability, CI/CD, Fluid Compute, workflows, AI SDK, AI Gateway, Sandbox, and agent tooling.
pitch.credentialLine: Vercel cites customers shipping 73,000+ deployments in a month, serving 350M monthly users, launching MVPs in six weeks, and running over 92B requests per day across its global edge.
pitch.ctaStyle: Offer a focused technical review: identify one high-friction release, performance, AI-agent, or custom-domain workflow and map what would change on Vercel in 30 minutes.

framingLibrary: Teams shipping AI features often find release speed is limited by infrastructure work.
Traffic spikes tend to expose performance and scaling gaps at the worst moment.
Growing frontend teams often spend more time on build and preview setup than on product work.
closingQuestions: Worth a quick look at where this could shorten your release cycle?
Open to comparing how your team handles previews and rollbacks today?
Would a short technical review of one release workflow be useful?

objectionTemplates: If the team already has CI/CD, position around reducing custom staging, preview, rollback, governance, and web-performance work rather than replacing every pipeline.
If they worry about usage-based costs, lead with spend management, usage alerts, Flat Rate CDN options, and enterprise contract controls.
If security is the blocker, anchor on SSO, audit logs, protected deployments, firewall, compliance programs, and private networking options for enterprise teams.
